response.assayComponentEndpointDesc: Data from the assay component TOX21_AChE_ms_Antagonist was analyzed into 1 assay endpoint. This assay endpoint, TOX21_AChE_ms_Antagonist, was analyzed in the positive analysis fitting direction relative to DMSO as the negative control and baseline of activity. Using a type of inducible reporter, loss-of-signal activity can be used to understand changes in enzymatic activity. To generalize the intended target to other relatable targets, this assay endpoint is annotated to the esterase intended target family, where the subfamily is acetylcholinesterase.
response.assayComponentDesc: TOX21_AChE_ms_Antagonist is an assay readout measuring inhibition of human recombinant acetylcholinesterase activity in a biochemical format using a colorimetric substrate.
response.assayComponentTargetDesc: The assay uses 5, 5-dithiobis-(2-nitrobenzoic acid) (DTNB) to quantify the thiocholine produced from the hydrolysis of acetylthiocholine by AChE. AChE hydrolyses the acetylthiocholine to produce thiocholine that in turn reduces the DTNB, producing 5-thio-2-nitrobenzoic acid (TNB) which absorbs at 405 nm.
response.assayDesc: TOX21_AChE_ms_Antagonist is a cell-free assay that uses recombinant human AChE (acetylcholinesterase) mixed with human liver microsomes as a source for enzyme to evaluate compounds that need metabolic activation for AChE inhibition, with measurements taken 30 minutes after compound dosing in a 1536-well plate. See tox21-ms-ache-p2.
response.assaySourceLongName: Toxicology in the 21st Century federal research collaboration
response.assaySourceDesc: The Toxicology in the 21st Century (Tox21) program aims to develop better toxicity assessment methods to quickly and efficiently test whether certain chemical compounds have the potential to disrupt processes in the human body that may lead to negative health effects. The Tox21 consortium is a federal collaboration between EPA, the National Toxicology Program (NTP) headquartered at the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The NIH Chemical Genomics Center (NCGC) is the primary screening facility running ultra high-throughput screening assays across a large interagency-developed chemical library, often referred to as the Tox21 10K Library.
